howItWorks.sub: Pick an example below and watch it go from a request to a finished run.

describe.title: Describe it
describe.body: Brief it like a colleague: what to do, when, with which accounts. Toone drafts the routine and decides which steps a script can do and which need an agent.

run.title: Watch it run
run.body: Automatic steps are scripts: they run the fixed parts exactly, with no agent and no tokens. Agents take the steps that need judgment, each on the model you picked. Every step lights up as it runs.

resume.body: Each step has a contract: a check its output must pass. A step that falls short retries, switches to a fallback or pauses and asks you. Edit it in plain words and resume where it stopped.

faq.title: What people ask us first
faq.sub: Short answers. The <link>product guide</link> goes deeper.
faq.a1: Toone is a Mac app that turns work you repeat into routines. You describe the work in plain words; Toone drafts the routine, runs the steps that never change as scripts and gives the steps that need judgment to AI agents on your own Claude Code or Codex. You watch every run live and can pause, edit and resume it.
faq.q2: Is Toone just n8n with AI?
faq.a2: No. In n8n, Make or Zapier you wire each node by hand, and AI is one node in the flow. In Toone you describe the work and it builds the routine: scripts for the parts that never change, agents for the parts that need judgment, and a contract on every output. For app-to-app syncs that must run around the clock, n8n, Make or Zapier fit better: Toone runs while your Mac is awake.
faq.a3: Automatic steps are scripts, so they don’t touch your AI plan. Agent steps use the Claude or ChatGPT plan you already pay for, through Claude Code or Codex. There is no separate AI plan to buy from us. Paid services a step calls, like Semrush, bill you as usual. Running routines is never limited.
faq.q4: Do I need to write code?
faq.a4: No. You describe the routine and Toone writes the scripts for its automatic steps. To change a step, describe the change; Toone updates the routine and you check it before it runs.
faq.q5: Which tools can Toone work with?
faq.a5: Any service with an API, tools connected through MCP (the standard way AI apps plug into other tools), and websites, through a browser inside Toone where you sign in with your own accounts.
faq.q6: What happens when a step fails or falls short?
faq.a6: Contracts check each step’s output. A step that falls short retries, switches to a fallback or pauses and asks you, depending on the rule you set. Edit it in plain words and resume where it stopped; finished steps keep their results.
faq.q7: Where does it run, and where is my data?
faq.a7: On your Mac. Routines, run history and project files stay on your machine. Agent steps send what they work on to Anthropic or OpenAI through your own Claude Code or Codex, under your plan’s terms. Steps that send, post or pay can wait for your approval.
faq.q8: What if my Mac is asleep when a routine is due?
faq.a8: Scheduled routines need your Mac awake with Toone open. A run that falls due while it sleeps isn’t lost: it runs once when the Mac is next awake, then the routine goes back to its usual schedule.
faq.q9: Is Toone free? What does Toone Pro add?
faq.a9: Yes. Every account can create {free} routines for free, and running routines is never limited. Toone Pro removes the limit on creating routines, with a monthly, a yearly or a single lifetime payment. Plans and prices are on the pricing page.
faq.a10: Create an account on trytoone.com and download Toone for your Mac. Start from a ready-made routine on Explore or describe your own; the guided setup takes you to a first run in about fifteen minutes. If you have a code, redeem it at trytoone.com/redeem.

explore.aboutWhat: Explore is Toone's public library of routine and workflow templates. People share routines they already run in their own work, across professions and use cases, so you can start from a process that works instead of an empty page. A routine is one repeatable job, and a bundle groups routines that belong together. Each listing explains the outcome, who it is for, how the work is broken down and what it needs from you before it runs.
explore.aboutReview: Toone reviews every listing before it appears here. Shared copies have personal details removed and are checked for secrets, private data and unsafe instructions. Listings are free to use, and adding one to your organization never overwrites your existing agents, Skills or routines.
